body: You reference macOS in the system information but the rest is about iOS, can you provide the iOS version you are testing this on?

Because I've seen my own game's name (Lost For Swords) I tried to replicate it on my end. And it actually crashed for me when quickly tapping the splash screen before the game itself shows up! Nooo!!! (huge thanks for finding this and name dropping my game to let me find it too @SinghSamrat )

I tested using a testflight build, and got a different behavior (crash instead of freeze), but nevertheless a bug! Can reproduce it 100% if I'm quick enough to tap the screen before the splash screen is gone.

Here's my iPad info I tested on:
```
"deviceModel" : "iPad14,8",
"osVersion" : "18.1.1",
```

The game is built using Godot 3.6.stable.

I was able to mitigate a similar crash in my case by setting "debug/disable_touch" to true from project settings and disabling it only after my app reaches Home Screen, but the freeze issue is still present. In the Godot source code, "OSIPhone::touch_press" function seems to not process any input if "debug/disable_touch" is true.

That workaround did indeed fix the crash bug for me as well! The settings flag is apparently not documented at all, but I checked that it exists in the 3.6 source. It explicitly makes `OSIPhone::touch_press` and `OSIPhone::touch_drag` return early and into a no-op.

I can now reproduce your original bug: when tapping on the splash screen, the game becomes unresponsive to touch input. It does not happen every time though and I've not found a deterministic pattern yet. Also it fixes itself when I go back to the home screen and then return to the game.

I'm not even sure I like the workaround that much, because I almost rather have the game crash and let people open it again, than being unresponsive. But either way, it's a less than ideal situation :(

I just faced the same issue and fixed it by forcibly clearing the stuck touch state after the splash screen using a synthetic touch release event.

``` gdscript
# main.tscn

func _ready() -> void:
	# Fix stuck touch state after splash screen
	Input.parse_input_event(create_release_event())

func create_release_event() -> InputEventScreenTouch:
	"""Create a release event to clear stuck touch state after splash screen on iOS."""
	var release_event = InputEventScreenTouch.new()
	release_event.pressed = false
	release_event.index = 0
	release_event.position = Vector2.ZERO
	return release_event
```
